+      # Prove the published jar is usable BEFORE publishing it, by exercising it

+      # classpath and no scala-library anywhere.
+      #
+      # This is the guard that was missing. A previous release shipped a parser
+      # jar that could not be compiled against at all and failed at runtime with
+      # NoSuchMethodError on ReadAst$Root, and nothing in the pipeline noticed.
+      - name: Verify the published jar is consumable
+        env:
+          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ needs.validate.outputs.tag }}
+        run: |
+          set -euo pipefail
+          JAR="tools/shade/build/libs/flix-parser-${RELEASE_TAG}.jar"
+
+          # List the entries once and grep the file, rather than piping unzip into
+          # grep. Under `set -o pipefail`, `grep -q` exits on its first match and
+          # unzip dies of SIGPIPE, so the pipeline reports failure precisely when
+          # the pattern IS found -- which inverts both checks below and makes the
+          # unshaded-scala one incapable of ever firing.
+          unzip -Z1 "$JAR" > entries.txt
+
+          # Scala must be fully relocated; a stray unshaded entry would collide
+          # with the consumer's own Scala.
+          if grep -qE '^scala/' entries.txt; then
+            echo "Shaded jar still contains unshaded scala/**." >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+          # ...and the facade must NOT have been relocated, or the entry point moved.
+          if ! grep -q '^org/openrewrite/flix/spi/' entries.txt; then
+            echo "Shaded jar has no facade; consumers have no entry point." >&2
+            exit 1
+          fi
+
+          mkdir -p probe
+          cat > Probe.java <<'JAVA'
+          import org.openrewrite.flix.spi.FlixCstElement;
+          import org.openrewrite.flix.spi.FlixCstNode;
+          import org.openrewrite.flix.spi.FlixCstToken;
+          import org.openrewrite.flix.spi.FlixFrontEnd;
+          import org.openrewrite.flix.spi.FlixParseResult;
+
+          public class Probe {
+              public static void main(String[] args) {
+                  String source = "def main(): Unit \\ IO = println(\"hi\")\n";
+                  FlixParseResult result = FlixFrontEnd.parse("Probe.flix", source);
+                  if (!result.getDiagnostics().isEmpty()) {
+                      throw new AssertionError("unexpected diagnostics: " + result.getDiagnostics());
+                  }
+                  // Reconstructing the source from token offsets proves the CST covers
+                  // the file, which is what lossless printing depends on.
+                  StringBuilder out = new StringBuilder();
+                  int[] cursor = {0};
+                  rebuild(result.getTree(), source, out, cursor);
+                  out.append(source.substring(cursor[0]));
+                  if (!out.toString().equals(source)) {
+                      throw new AssertionError("round trip differed: " + out);
+                  }
+                  System.out.println("parser jar is consumable from plain Java");
+              }
+
+              static void rebuild(FlixCstElement e, String src, StringBuilder out, int[] cursor) {
+                  if (e instanceof FlixCstToken) {
+                      FlixCstToken t = (FlixCstToken) e;
+                      out.append(src, cursor[0], t.getStart()).append(src, t.getStart(), t.getEnd());
+                      cursor[0] = t.getEnd();
+                      return;
+                  }
+                  for (FlixCstElement c : ((FlixCstNode) e).getChildren()) {
+                      rebuild(c, src, out, cursor);
+                  }
+              }
+          }
+          JAVA
+
+          javac -cp "$JAR" -d probe Probe.java
+          java -cp "probe:$JAR" Probe

+compiler), one generic, versioned `flix-parser-*.jar` (the slim, Scala-shaded
+front-end parser consumed by `rewrite-flix`), and one generic, versioned
+local-Maven bundle on Linux AMD64, plus a checksum manifest. Consumers verify
+the generic files; they do not select a platform variant.
+
+### How `flix-parser-*.jar` is built, and why
+
+1. The **facade** in `facade/src` is compiled against the Flix assembly. It is a
+   handful of plain-Java types plus a Scala object whose only entry point,
+   `org.openrewrite.flix.spi.FlixFrontEnd.parse`, takes and returns Java types.
+2. The result is merged into the assembly and shrunk with ProGuard
+   (`flix-facade.pro`), seeded only at the facade, which drops the
+   Weeder/Resolver/Typer and the JVM backend.
+3. Scala is relocated into `org.openrewrite.flix.shaded.scala` with Gradle
+   Shadow (`tools/shade`).
+
+The facade is why this works. Shading rewrites the Flix front-end's own public
+signatures — `Lexer.run` would take a relocated `Map` — so a consumer compiled
+against the real Scala library fails at runtime with `NoSuchMethodError`, and
+shading the consumer too is impossible: scalac hardwires `scala.Any` and
+refuses to compile against a relocated standard library. Because the boundary
+carries only Java types, the relocation is invisible and **consumers need no
+Scala dependency at all**.
+

+classes, so pickle signatures need not survive, and the artifact can be both
+aggressively shrunk and shaded. A final workflow step runs the published jar
+from plain Java with no scala-library on the classpath, so an unusable artifact
+cannot be released again.

+`Lexer.run`/`Parser2.run` from the `Flix` god-object; without it the whole
+compiler is reachable and nothing shrinks.

@@ -1,39 +0,0 @@
-# ProGuard rules for the compile-time ("API") Flix parser artifact.
-#
-# Why this exists as a SECOND shrink, rather than reusing the R8 output:
-#
-#   R8 removes every Scala pickle signature. Scala 2.13 carries a class's type
-#   information in a `@scala.reflect.ScalaSignature` annotation, and R8 drops
-#   annotation instances whose annotation *type* was shrunk away -- and then
-#   drops them even when that type is explicitly kept and `-keepattributes *`
-#   is in force (measured: 0 of 200 sampled ca.uwaterloo.flix.language.ast
-#   classes retained ScalaSignature). Without the pickle, scalac reads the Flix
-#   classes as plain Java classes, so case-class companions fail to resolve
-#   ("Input.VirtualFile is not a value") and the consumer cannot compile.
-#
-#   ProGuard retains ScalaSignature under the same rules, so it -- not R8 --
-#   produces the compile-time artifact. R8 still produces the runtime artifact
-#   (flix-parser.pro): it is smaller, and only its bytecode has to run.
-#
-# Two further constraints, both established by experiment:
-#
-#   * The retained `scala/**` subset must be excluded. A partial scala-library
-#     on the compile classpath makes scalac fail to build its symbol table
-#     ("Missing dependency 'object scala.native'"). The consumer supplies a
-#     complete org.scala-lang:scala-library instead.
-#   * All non-class resources must be excluded. A root `library.properties`
-#     alone makes scalac misidentify this jar as the Scala library.
-#
-# `-dontoptimize` keeps the artifact a faithful ABI of the assembly; nothing
-# here is ever executed, so there is nothing to gain from optimising it.
-
--include flix-parser.pro
-
--dontoptimize
-
-# The pickle carriers. Keeping the annotation types is necessary (though, for
-# R8, not sufficient) for the ScalaSignature annotations to survive shrinking.
--keep class scala.reflect.ScalaSignature { *; }
--keep class scala.reflect.ScalaLongSignature { *; }
-
--keepattributes RuntimeVisibleAnnotations,RuntimeInvisibleAnnotations,Signature,Scala,ScalaSig,ScalaInlineInfo
